name: Abu Dhabi
title: UTM Thickness Gauging in Abu Dhabi: Hull & OSV Inspection
description: Thickness measurement in Abu Dhabi at Khalifa Port, Zayed Port and Mussafah: hull structure gauging, renewal survey scopes and offshore vessel UTM.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships and Offshore Vessels in Abu Dhabi
intro: Abu Dhabi combines a large container and industrial port at Khalifa with a substantial offshore oil and gas support fleet. Supply vessels, crew boats, liftboats and accommodation units working the emirate's offshore fields need hull and tank gauging at every renewal survey, and tankers loading at the western terminals face CAP and vetting requirements. Our ultrasonic thickness measurement in Abu Dhabi is delivered by technicians who travel from India to the vessel, slipway or repair berth.
keywords: ultrasonic thickness measurement in abu dhabi

highlights.h: OSV thickness gauging on short slipways
highlights.p: Supply vessels and crew boats at Mussafah are often slipped for only a few days. We start on the bottom shell and sea chests while access is open, then follow tank cleaning so the repair list is ready early.

Self-propelled liftboats and accommodation barges have leg wells, jacking structure and preload tanks that a ship-type TM plan misses. We build the plan around the unit's own structural arrangement and its class survey requirements.

Crude and product tankers lifting cargo off the western coast are vetted like anywhere else. Gauging at anchorage gives the owner deck, ballast-tank and cargo-tank evidence for a CAP rating or a charterer's review.

port.h: Abu Dhabi's ports, terminals and offshore fleet
p: Abu Dhabi's commercial shipping is spread along a long coastline. Khalifa Port, run by AD Ports Group at Taweelah between the capital and Dubai, is the emirate's main container and industrial gateway, with deep-water berths serving container lines and the industrial and free zones behind it. Zayed Port in the city handles general cargo, ro-ro and the cruise terminal. West of the capital, the Ruwais industrial complex and the crude-oil loading terminals export the emirate's oil, refined products and LPG, and Das Island has long been the base of Abu Dhabi's LNG exports.

The offshore sector shapes inspection demand more than anything else. Abu Dhabi's offshore oil and gas fields are served by a large fleet of platform supply vessels, anchor-handling tugs, crew boats, self-propelled liftboats, accommodation barges and landing craft, much of it operating from Mussafah and the emirate's offshore logistics bases. These vessels work continuously in shallow, warm water, often for years on long-term charters, and come into a yard only when the renewal or docking survey falls due. That compresses gauging, steel repair and the survey into one short window, and makes preparation before the vessel arrives worth more than extra hands once it is on the slip.

Deep-sea ships also stay long enough to gauge. Tankers sometimes wait off the western terminals for loading windows, container ships and car carriers have scheduled calls at Khalifa Port, and multipurpose and break-bulk ships carrying project cargo and steel for the industrial zones can spend several days alongside. Tankers lifting Abu Dhabi crude and products are screened by charterers and oil-major vetting in the usual way, which keeps CAP gauging and condition records on the agenda for older ships calling at the western terminals. For owners managing both an offshore fleet and deep-sea tonnage from the capital, one trip from India can often take in more than one vessel.

facilities.h: Where we gauge in Abu Dhabi: yards, berths and offshore bases
p: Most offshore-vessel thickness measurement at Mussafah takes place at the repair yards and marine bases along the Mussafah channel, which is lined with fabrication shops, workboat yards and slipways. Many of these vessels are docked on slipways or shiplifts rather than in a graving dock, so access to the bottom shell is good but the time out of the water is short. We work alongside the repair contractor so that readings on bottom plating, sea chests, the stern frame area and thruster tunnels are taken before blasting and painting crews move in.

Deep-sea ships are gauged at berths in Khalifa Port and Zayed Port, or at the anchorages off Abu Dhabi, when the scope is limited to piping, decks or a sample of tanks. Full renewal-survey programmes on large tankers and gas carriers need a dock, and when a ship owned or managed from Abu Dhabi docks elsewhere in the Gulf, we follow it to that yard. For offshore units between charters, idle time alongside is often the most practical gauging window of all, because the crew is available and the deck is clear of cargo.
list: Mussafah marine and offshore yards — renewal-survey gauging of supply vessels, crew boats, landing craft and liftboats on slipways, shiplifts and repair berths
Khalifa Port — hull gauging at Khalifa Port berths on boxships, vehicle carriers and multipurpose vessels during longer stays, with ISPS access arranged through the agent
Zayed Port — piping and deck gauging on ro-ro, general cargo and cruise ships alongside the city berths, fitted around cargo and passenger operations
Ruwais and the western terminals — gauging on product tankers and gas carriers at anchorage or lay-by, within the terminal operator's safety and permit rules
Stood-down offshore units — gauging of accommodation barges, liftboats and jack-up hulls during idle periods between charters, when tanks can be emptied and ventilated
Abu Dhabi anchorages — pre-purchase and on-hire condition checks of tankers and dry bulk ships, boarded from a launch the agent arranges

context.h: Regulation, ownership and the offshore market in Abu Dhabi
p: Port state control at Abu Dhabi follows the Riyadh MoU, the regime shared by the GCC states. Offshore support vessels are classed and surveyed like any other ship, with annual, intermediate and renewal surveys under the class society's rules, but their charterers add inspection regimes of their own, and offshore vetting through OCIMF's OVID scheme puts hull and deck condition under scrutiny before a vessel is accepted. No emission control area covers the Gulf, so MARPOL Annex VI's global 0.50% sulphur limit applies; the OSV fleet typically burns marine gas oil, so its corrosion problems sit in the hull, tanks and seawater systems rather than in scrubber piping.

Abu Dhabi is home to a large state-linked shipping and offshore logistics sector serving the national oil company, alongside private owners and managers running tankers, bulk carriers and workboats. The physical environment favours corrosion. Shallow coastal waters around the offshore fields are warm and saline, sediment and marine growth build up in sea chests and seawater cooling lines, and the cargo decks of supply vessels take constant abrasion and impact from pipe and container handling. Drill-water, brine, mud and fuel tanks on these ships corrode at very different rates, which is why a sound gauging plan samples each tank type separately rather than averaging across them.

jobs.h: Typical gauging work in Abu Dhabi
jobs.p: Abu Dhabi enquiries split between the offshore fleet, where gauging is usually part of a short yard period, and deep-sea ships at Khalifa Port or the western terminals, where it is driven by sale, charter or vetting. The scenarios below are representative, and each one is scheduled around the vessel's survey status and the time the yard, base or terminal allows on board.
list: Second renewal survey of a platform supply vessel on a Mussafah slipway: bottom and side shell, cargo deck, mud and brine tanks, and the stern area around the propeller and thruster tunnels.

OSV thickness gauging before a long-term charter: deck, tank and hull readings on an anchor-handling tug, so the charterer's inspector and the owner start the contract with an agreed condition record.
Pre-purchase gauging of a crew boat or landing craft offered for sale in Abu Dhabi, sampling the hull, deck and tanks to flag substantial corrosion before the buyer commits.
CAP gauging on a product tanker anchored off Ruwais, covering deck, cargo-tank and ballast-tank structure ahead of an oil-major vetting cycle.
Liftboat leg-well, jacking-structure and hull gauging during an idle period between campaigns, so the owner knows the steel condition before bidding for the next contract.

logistics: The team flies into Zayed International Airport (AUH), Abu Dhabi's main airport, with direct services from a number of Indian cities; Dubai's airports are a practical alternative for jobs near Khalifa Port. Access to the Mussafah yards is arranged with the yard and the owner, Khalifa Port and Zayed Port need ISPS passes applied for by the ship's agent, and anchorage or terminal work needs a launch booked the same way. UAE visas are arranged before departure, so we need the yard date or the ship's ETA early, and we keep it under review as offshore schedules move.

faqs.q: Can you gauge an offshore supply vessel during a short slipway period in Mussafah?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is where planning matters most. We study the last TM report and the class survey requirements before the vessel is slipped, prepare a TM plan by compartment, and start with the bottom shell and sea chests while access is open. Tank readings follow as tanks are cleaned and gas-freed, so the repair contractor receives the renewal list early in the slipway period.

faqs.q: Do you carry out ship inspection in Abu Dhabi for tankers at the western terminals?
faqs.a: Limited scopes, yes: deck plating, piping, accessible ballast tanks and sample cargo tanks when the ship is at anchorage with gas-free spaces. Terminal berths have their own permit-to-work rules, and gauging alongside during cargo operations is rarely allowed, so we plan anchorage work with the agent and the terminal's marine department well before the team flies.

faqs.q: What corrodes fastest on supply vessels working Abu Dhabi's fields?
faqs.a: Cargo deck plating under pipe and container handling, the stern area around roller and towing gear, sea chests and seawater cooling lines fouled by marine growth, and tanks that alternate between drill water, brine and ballast. Warm, saline coastal water accelerates all of it, which is why vessels on long charters can show substantial corrosion well before their age would suggest.

faqs.q: Do liftboats and accommodation barges need thickness measurement?
faqs.a: Yes. Liftboats and accommodation barges are classed and surveyed, and their renewal surveys include gauging of the hull, deck, preload and ballast tanks, and the structure around the leg wells and jacking system. Units that spend long periods jacked up in the same field see uneven corrosion where the legs pass through the splash zone and in tanks that are rarely emptied, so a targeted TM plan matters.
